answers.brief_reasoning: Standard procedure
answers.final_answer: Equipment: a power supply, an ammeter in series with the wire, a voltmeter across the wire (or just an ohmmeter), a meter stick, and a micrometer to check d. Clamp the wire straight along the meter stick. Put one fixed contact at the zero mark and a sliding contact (crocodile clip) at distance L. Set L to 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 m by moving the clip. At each length, measure V and I and calculate R = V/I. Keep the current small so the wire does not heat up and change its resistance. To reduce uncertainty in R: repeat each reading several times (or take several V–I pairs and use the slope) and average. Also subtract the resistance of the leads, measured with the clips touching.
